**The meaning of the verse**
﴿وَالَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُوا الدَّارَ وَالْإِيمَانَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ يُحِبُّونَ مَنْ هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمْ حَاجَةً مِّمَّا أُوتُوا وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَلَوْ كَانَ بِهِمْ خَصَاصَةٌ ۚ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ فَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾

And those who settled in Madinah and believed before the Muhajirun emigrated — they are the Ansar — love the Muhajirun and share their wealth with them, and they find in themselves no envy of them for what they were given of the fay' wealth and other things. They put the Muhajirun and those in need before themselves, even if they themselves are in need and poverty. And whoever is saved from stinginess and from holding back surplus wealth, those are the successful, who have attained what they sought.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What was in front of Hadi when Abu Subhi knocked on the door? And why did his mother leave the decision to him?
2. How did Hadi answer when the old man asked him, "And what about you?"
3. Must a person always give away all their food? (No; putting others first is a virtue, not an obligation, and a person must not neglect those they provide for. Here the mother was content, and there were three of them together while the old man was alone.)

**This week's exercise**
At a family meal this week, your child serves the dish to others before themselves, and leaves the best piece for someone else without announcing it. Then they carry a dish with you to an elderly or needy neighbour.
